explanation: Hebrews 11:29 states 'By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land,' emphasizing faith as the key element.

question: Complete this verse from Hebrews: 'It is appointed for men to die once, but after this the _____.'
hint: This refers to what happens after death when God evaluates our lives.
explanation: Hebrews 9:27 says 'Just as people are destined to die once, and after that to face judgment.'

question: What did Jesus do when he entered the Most Holy Place?
hint: He brought something that was part of himself, not from animals.
explanation: Hebrews 9:12 explains that Jesus entered the Most Holy Place once for all by his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.

question: According to Hebrews 12, believers have come to Mount _____, the city of the living God.
hint: This is the heavenly mountain, not an earthly one where the law was given.
explanation: Hebrews 12:22 states 'But you have come to Mount Zion, to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem.'

question: Who does Hebrews say was 'without father or mother, without genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life'?
hint: This mysterious priest-king appears briefly in Genesis and is used as a type of Christ.
explanation: Hebrews 7:3 describes Melchizedek as 'Without father or mother, without genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, resembling the Son of God.'

question: According to Hebrews, what makes the new covenant superior to the old?
hint: The superiority lies in what God has promised.
explanation: Hebrews 8:6 states that Jesus is the mediator of a better covenant, which is established on better promises.

question: According to Hebrews, why was it necessary for Christ to be made like his brothers in every way?
options: To make atonement for the sins of the people
hint: This relates to his priestly function and dealing with sin.
explanation: Hebrews 2:17 explains that he had to be made like them, fully human in every way, in order that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, and that he might make atonement for the sins of the people.

question: According to Hebrews, who created the worlds?
hint: This person is described as the heir of all things in Hebrews 1.
explanation: Hebrews 1:2 states that God has spoken to us by his Son, through whom he made the universe.

question: Complete this verse: 'Do not forget to show _____ to strangers.'
hint: This virtue involves welcoming people into your home.
explanation: Hebrews 13:2 says 'Do not forget to show hospitality to strangers, for by so doing some people have shown hospitality to angels without knowing it.'

question: What did Sarah do by faith despite her old age?
hint: This involved bringing new life into the world when it seemed impossible.
explanation: Hebrews 11:11 states that by faith Sarah, even though she was past childbearing age, was enabled to bear children because she considered him faithful who had made the promise.

question: Who refused to be known as the son of Pharaoh's daughter?
hint: This person led the Israelites out of Egypt.
explanation: Hebrews 11:24 says 'By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be known as the son of Pharaoh's daughter.'

question: According to Hebrews, what does God discipline us for?
hint: The purpose is positive and beneficial for us.
explanation: Hebrews 12:10 states that God disciplines us for our good, in order that we may share in his holiness.

question: What happened when the Israelites tried to cross the Red Sea by faith?
options: They passed through on dry ground
hint: The outcome was successful due to their faith.
explanation: Hebrews 11:29 says 'By faith the people passed through the Red Sea as on dry land; but when the Egyptians tried to do so, they were drowned.'

question: Complete this warning: 'It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the _____ God.'
hint: This describes God's eternal nature.
explanation: Hebrews 10:31 warns 'It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.'

question: According to Hebrews, what city did Abraham look forward to?
options: A city with foundations whose architect and builder is God
hint: This city has a divine architect and builder.
explanation: Hebrews 11:10 states that Abraham was looking forward to the city with foundations, whose architect and builder is God.

question: Who prostitute was saved when Jericho was conquered because she welcomed the spies?
hint: This person helped the Israelite spies in Jericho.
explanation: Hebrews 11:31 mentions 'By faith the prostitute Rahab, because she welcomed the spies, was not killed with those who were disobedient.'

question: What does Hebrews say Christ will do when he appears a second time?
options: Bring salvation to those who are waiting for him
hint: This relates specifically to those who eagerly await his return.
explanation: Hebrews 9:28 says 'so Christ was sacrificed once to take away the sins of many; and he will appear a second time, not to bear sin, but to bring salvation to those who are waiting for him.'

question: Complete this verse: 'And without faith it is impossible to _____ God.'
hint: This verse is about what God desires from those who come to Him.
explanation: Hebrews 11:6 states 'And without faith it is impossible to please God, because anyone who comes to him must believe that he exists and that he rewards those who earnestly seek him.'

question: According to Hebrews, who are the 'cloud of witnesses' that surrounds believers?
options: The faithful people listed in chapter 11
hint: These are people who demonstrated faith throughout history.
explanation: Hebrews 12:1 refers to the great cloud of witnesses as the faithful people described in Hebrews 11 who lived by faith.

question: Who does Hebrews say appointed Jesus as a Son over God's house?
hint: Think about who has the authority to appoint Jesus as Son.
explanation: Hebrews 3:6 states that Christ is faithful as the Son over God's house, appointed by God the Father.

question: What did Isaac do by faith according to Hebrews 11?
hint: This involved Isaac's two sons and their future.
explanation: Hebrews 11:20 says 'By faith Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau in regard to their future.'

question: According to Hebrews, what happens to those who have once been enlightened but then fall away?
options: It is impossible to bring them back to repentance
They are given more time to decide
hint: This passage describes a very serious spiritual condition.
explanation: Hebrews 6:4-6 states it is impossible for those who have fallen away to be brought back to repentance.

question: According to Hebrews, what mountain represents the old covenant that believers have NOT come to?
hint: This mountain was associated with the giving of the Law and was a place of fear.
explanation: Hebrews 12:18 refers to Mount Sinai as the fearsome mountain of the old covenant, contrasted with Mount Zion.

question: According to Hebrews, what did the earthly tabernacle serve as?
options: A copy and shadow of heavenly things
A place for daily sacrifices only
hint: The earthly sanctuary was a representation of something greater in heaven.
explanation: Hebrews 8:5 explains that the earthly priests serve at a sanctuary that is a copy and shadow of what is in heaven.

question: According to James, who should we especially care for?
hint: Think about people who need the most help
explanation: James 1:27 defines pure religion as looking after orphans and widows in their distress.

question: According to James, what should we ask God for if we lack it?
hint: It helps us make good decisions
explanation: James 1:5 states that if any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault.

question: James says faith without what is dead?
hint: It means doing good things
explanation: James 2:26 declares that faith without deeds (works) is dead.

question: What does James say about the tongue?
hint: Small things can be very strong
explanation: James 3:5 describes the tongue as a small part of the body that makes great boasts and can cause great damage.

question: According to James, what happens when we draw near to God?
hint: God responds the same way we approach Him
explanation: James 4:8 promises that if we come near to God, He will come near to us.

question: James warns against showing favoritism to people based on what?
hint: Think about rich and poor people
explanation: James 2:1-4 specifically warns against showing favoritism based on wealth, using the example of treating a rich person better than a poor person.

question: What does James say about testing and temptation?
options: Temptation comes from our own desires
hint: The problem starts inside us
explanation: James 1:14 explains that each person is tempted when dragged away by their own evil desire and enticed.

question: What attitude does James say we should have about our future plans?
hint: We should remember who is really in control
explanation: James 4:15 teaches that instead of boasting about tomorrow, we ought to say, 'If it is the Lord's will, we will live and do this or that.'

question: In James' discussion of wisdom, what are the characteristics of wisdom from above?
hint: Heavenly wisdom has many good qualities
explanation: James 3:17 describes wisdom from above as first pure, then peaceable, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, unwavering, without hypocrisy.

question: Which Old Testament figures does James mention as examples of faith and patience?
hint: One was a patriarch, one was from Jericho
explanation: James 2:21-25 mentions Abraham as an example of faith with works, and Rahab as an example of faith demonstrated through actions.

question: According to James, what is the relationship between friendship with the world and enmity with God?
options: Friendship with world makes enmity with God
hint: You cannot serve two masters
explanation: James 4:4 declares that friendship with the world means enmity against God, and whoever chooses to be a friend of the world becomes an enemy of God.

question: Who wrote the book of James?
hint: This person was the brother of Jesus
explanation: James, the brother of Jesus, is traditionally considered the author of this epistle.

question: According to James, what should elders do when someone is sick?
options: Tell them to see a doctor only
Pray over them and anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord
hint: James 5:14 gives specific instructions for church elders
explanation: James 5:14 instructs 'Are any of you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them and anoint them with oil in the name of the Lord.'

question: What does James call himself at the beginning of his letter?
options: A servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ
hint: He uses a humble title in James 1:1
explanation: James identifies himself as 'a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ' (James 1:1), showing humility despite being Jesus' brother.

question: According to James, what should we do when we face trials?
hint: James 1:2 tells us our attitude toward difficulties
explanation: James 1:2 says 'Consider it pure joy, my brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of many kinds.'

question: What does James say about being quick to listen?
options: Be quick to speak and slow to listen
Be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry
hint: This famous advice is in James 1:19
explanation: James 1:19 teaches 'Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry.'

question: According to James, what kind of religion does God accept?
hint: James 1:27 describes pure religion
explanation: James 1:27 states that pure religion includes 'to look after orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.'

question: What scenario does James use to illustrate favoritism in the assembly?
options: A rich person and a poor person entering
hint: James 2:2-3 describes this scene
explanation: James 2:2-3 describes a scenario where a rich person in fine clothes and a poor person in filthy clothes enter the assembly, and favoritism is shown to the rich person.

question: What does James say about double-minded people?
options: They are unstable in all they do
hint: James 1:8 describes their character
explanation: James 1:8 says 'Such a person is double-minded and unstable in all they do,' referring to those who doubt when they pray.

question: According to James, what does sin do when it is full-grown?
hint: James 1:15 describes sin's progression
explanation: James 1:15 states 'Then, after desire has conceived, it gives birth to sin; and sin, when it is full-grown, gives birth to death.'

question: What does James say about those who teach?
options: They will be judged more strictly
hint: James 3:1 warns about teaching responsibility
explanation: James 3:1 warns 'Not many of you should become teachers, my fellow believers, because you know that we who teach will be judged more strictly.'

question: What does James say causes fights and quarrels among believers?
hint: James 4:1 identifies the source of conflicts
explanation: James 4:1 asks 'What causes fights and quarrels among you? Don't they come from your desires that battle within you?'

question: In James' teaching about the tongue, what does he say about blessing and cursing?
options: Both should come from different sources
Both blessing and cursing come from the same mouth, but this should not be
hint: James 3:9-10 addresses this contradiction
explanation: James 3:9-10 says 'With the tongue we praise our Lord and Father, and with it we curse human beings... Out of the same mouth come praise and cursing. My brothers and sisters, this should not be.'

question: What does James say about the rich who have hoarded wealth in the last days?
options: Their gold and silver are corroded and will testify against them
They should give everything away immediately
hint: James 5:3 describes the fate of hoarded wealth
explanation: James 5:3 states 'Your gold and silver are corroded. Their corrosion will testify against you and eat your flesh like fire. You have hoarded wealth in the last days.'

question: What does James say about the crown of life?
options: It's promised to those who love God and persevere under trial
hint: James 1:12 connects this crown to enduring trials
explanation: James 1:12 states that blessed is the one who perseveres under trial because, having stood the test, that person will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.

question: What does James say every good and perfect gift comes from?
options: From above, from the Father of lights
hint: James 1:17 talks about where good gifts originate
explanation: James 1:17 states that every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights, who does not change like shifting shadows.

question: According to James, what should we be slow to do?
options: Slow to speak and slow to anger
hint: This is part of James' advice about listening and responding
explanation: James 1:19 instructs believers to be quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry, because human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.

question: What does James say about looking at yourself in a mirror?
options: It helps you remember God's word
Forgetting what you look like is like hearing but not doing God's word
hint: James uses this as an illustration about hearing and doing
explanation: In James 1:23-24, James compares someone who hears the word but doesn't do what it says to someone who looks at their face in a mirror and immediately forgets what they look like.

question: What does James say we should do instead of just listening to the word?
hint: James emphasizes action, not just hearing
explanation: James 1:22 commands believers to be doers of the word, and not hearers only, otherwise they deceive themselves.

question: What does James say about merchants who plan their business without acknowledging God?
options: They should say 'If it is the Lord's will, we will do this or that'
hint: James 4:13-15 addresses presumptuous planning
explanation: James 4:15 teaches that instead of boasting about tomorrow's plans, we ought to say, 'If it is the Lord's will, we will live and do this or that.'

question: Which prophet does James mention as an example of patient suffering?
hint: This prophet prayed earnestly about rain
explanation: James 5:17 mentions Elijah as an example, noting that he was a human being just like us, and he prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain for three and a half years.

question: What does James say about swearing oaths?
options: Let your 'Yes' be yes, and your 'No' be no
hint: James 5:12 gives simple instruction about speech
explanation: James 5:12 instructs believers not to swear by heaven or earth or anything else, but to let their 'Yes' be yes, and their 'No,' no, or they will be condemned.

question: According to James, what should someone do if they have sinned?
options: Confess their sins to each other
hint: James 5:16 talks about confession and prayer
explanation: James 5:16 says to confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed, emphasizing that the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective.

question: What does James say about anyone who turns a sinner from the error of their way?
options: They will be rewarded in heaven
They will save them from death and cover a multitude of sins
hint: This is the final verse of James' letter
explanation: James 5:20 concludes the letter by stating that whoever turns a sinner from the error of their way will save them from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

question: How does James describe the wisdom that comes from heaven in contrast to earthly wisdom?
options: It is first pure, then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere
hint: James 3:17 lists multiple characteristics of heavenly wisdom
explanation: James 3:17 describes wisdom from heaven as first of all pure; then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere, contrasting it with earthly wisdom that is characterized by bitter envy and selfish ambition.

question: According to Peter, what is more precious than gold?
hint: It's something that can be tested by trials
explanation: 1 Peter 1:7 says that faith 'of greater worth than gold, which perishes even though refined by fire' may result in praise and glory when Jesus is revealed.

question: In Peter's teaching about submission, what specific situation does he address regarding suffering?
hint: It's better to suffer for one kind of action than another
explanation: 1 Peter 3:17 states 'It is better, if it is God's will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil,' emphasizing righteous suffering over deserved punishment.

question: Who wrote the book of 1 Peter?
hint: This apostle was also called Simon and walked on water
explanation: Peter, one of Jesus' twelve apostles, wrote this letter to encourage Christians facing persecution.

question: Who does Peter call 'a chosen people, a royal priesthood'?
hint: This refers to everyone who believes in Jesus
explanation: In 1 Peter 2:9, Peter describes all Christians as 'a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's special possession.'

question: According to 1 Peter, what should we cast on God?
hint: It's something that worries us
explanation: 1 Peter 5:7 says 'Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.'

question: What does Peter say Jesus did for our sins?
hint: Jesus carried something heavy for us
explanation: 1 Peter 2:24 states that Jesus 'bore our sins in his body on the cross, so that we might die to sins and live for righteousness.'

question: What does Peter compare the devil to?
hint: This animal is known as the king of beasts
explanation: 1 Peter 5:8 warns that 'your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion looking for someone to devour.'

question: Peter quotes which Old Testament passage about Jesus being a cornerstone?
hint: One book is known for prophecies about the Messiah, the other for songs
explanation: In 1 Peter 2:6-8, Peter quotes from Isaiah 28:16 and Psalm 118:22 about Jesus as the cornerstone that some will stumble over.

question: What does Peter say about the prophets who searched concerning salvation?
options: They searched about the grace coming to us
They were confused and gave up
They only wrote for their own time
hint: They investigated something that would come later
explanation: 1 Peter 1:10-12 explains that the prophets 'searched intently and with the greatest care' about 'the grace that was to come to you,' serving not themselves but future believers.

question: Who does Peter mention as his co-worker in writing this letter?
hint: This person is also known by a Latin name
explanation: In 1 Peter 5:12, Peter mentions 'Silas, whom I regard as a faithful brother' as helping him write the letter.

question: From which city does Peter say he is writing this letter?
hint: This is likely a code name for the capital of the Roman Empire
explanation: 1 Peter 5:13 mentions 'She who is in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends you her greetings.' Most scholars believe 'Babylon' refers to Rome.

question: What does Peter say happened to spirits in prison?
hint: Jesus went and proclaimed something to them
explanation: 1 Peter 3:19-20 describes how Jesus 'went and made proclamation to the imprisoned spirits' who disobeyed long ago in the days of Noah.

question: What does Peter say about the time when judgment begins?
hint: It begins with God's own people first
explanation: 1 Peter 4:17 states 'For it is time for judgment to begin with God's household; and if it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who do not obey the gospel of God?'

question: Who does Peter say believers should honor as the supreme authority?
hint: This person rules over a country
explanation: 1 Peter 2:17 says 'Show proper respect to everyone, love the family of believers, fear God, honor the emperor.'

question: According to Peter, what kind of milk should believers crave?
hint: It helps you grow spiritually
explanation: 1 Peter 2:2 states 'Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up in your salvation.'

question: What does Peter say Jesus did after He died?
hint: This happened on the third day
explanation: 1 Peter 1:3 mentions 'In his great mercy he has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead.'

question: What does Peter say all flesh is like?
hint: This grows in your yard and is green
explanation: 1 Peter 1:24 quotes 'All people are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall.'

question: According to Peter, who should wives be subject to?
hint: This is their marriage partner
explanation: 1 Peter 3:1 states 'Wives, in the same way submit yourselves to your own husbands so that, if any of them do not believe the word, they may be won over without words by the behavior of their wives.'

question: What does Peter say husbands should do regarding their wives?
hint: Treat them with understanding and honor
explanation: 1 Peter 3:7 says 'Husbands, in the same way be considerate as you live with your wives, and treat them with respect as the weaker partner and as heirs with you of the gracious gift of life.'

question: What does Peter say about suffering for doing good?
hint: God sees it as something positive
explanation: 1 Peter 3:14 states 'But even if you should suffer for what is right, you are blessed.'

question: What does Peter say love does?
hint: It hides or conceals something
explanation: 1 Peter 4:8 says 'Above all, love each other deeply, because love covers over a multitude of sins.'

question: To which regions does Peter address his letter?
options: Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia
hint: These are provinces in Asia Minor
explanation: 1 Peter 1:1 addresses the letter 'To God's elect, exiles scattered throughout the provinces of Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia.'

question: What does Peter call the elders in relation to Christ's sufferings?
hint: They saw or testified to what happened
explanation: 1 Peter 5:1 says 'To the elders among you, I appeal as a fellow elder and a witness of Christ's sufferings who also will share in the glory to be revealed.'

question: According to Peter, what happened when Christ was reviled?
options: He did not revile in return
hint: He showed restraint and didn't respond the same way
explanation: 1 Peter 2:23 states 'When they hurled their insults at him, he did not retaliate; when he suffered, he made no threats. Instead, he entrusted himself to him who judges justly.'

question: According to Peter, who is the Chief Shepherd?
hint: The one who died for our sins
explanation: In 1 Peter 5:4, Peter refers to Christ as 'the Chief Shepherd' who will appear and give crowns of glory.

question: What does Peter say God's people are chosen to do?
hint: It involves using your voice for God
explanation: 1 Peter 2:9 states that believers are chosen 'that you may declare the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.'

question: What does Peter say we should be prepared to give?
hint: It's about explaining what we believe
explanation: 1 Peter 3:15 instructs believers to 'always be prepared to give an answer to everyone who asks you to give the reason for the hope that you have.'

question: What does Peter say we should do to all people?
hint: It's about showing respect to everyone
explanation: 1 Peter 2:17 says 'Show proper respect to everyone, love the family of believers, fear God, honor the emperor.'

question: According to Peter, what will happen to those who do not obey the gospel?
hint: It's not a positive outcome
explanation: 1 Peter 4:17 asks 'what will the outcome be for those who do not obey the gospel of God?' implying judgment awaits them.

question: What does Peter say about the word of the Lord?
hint: Think about permanence
explanation: 1 Peter 1:25 quotes Isaiah, saying 'but the word of the Lord endures forever,' contrasting it with the temporary nature of human life.

question: What does Peter say Christ did to the spirits in prison?
hint: He went and made a proclamation
explanation: 1 Peter 3:19 states that Christ 'went and made proclamation to the imprisoned spirits,' which many interpret as preaching to them.

question: According to Peter, how should elders shepherd God's flock?
hint: It should come from the heart
explanation: 1 Peter 5:2 instructs elders to 'be shepherds of God's flock that is under your care, watching over them—not because you must, but because you are willing, as God wants you to be; not pursuing dishonest gain, but eager to serve.'

question: What does Peter say about judging others?
options: God will judge the living and dead
hint: Think about who has ultimate authority
explanation: 1 Peter 4:5 says that people 'will have to give account to him who is ready to judge the living and the dead.'

question: According to Peter, what was revealed to the prophets about their prophecies concerning salvation?
options: They were serving only their time
hint: Their prophecies had a future focus
explanation: 1 Peter 1:12 reveals 'It was revealed to them that they were not serving themselves but you, when they spoke of the things that have now been told you by those who have preached the gospel to you.'

question: What does Peter say about the relationship between baptism and salvation?
options: Baptism saves us through Christ's resurrection
hint: It connects to Christ's resurrection power
explanation: 1 Peter 3:21 states 'this water symbolizes baptism that now saves you also—not the removal of dirt from the body but the pledge of a clear conscience toward God. It saves you by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.'

question: Who wrote the book of 2 Peter?
hint: This apostle was also called Simon and had the keys to the kingdom.
explanation: The apostle Peter wrote 2 Peter, as stated in 2 Peter 1:1, identifying himself as 'Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ.'

question: According to 2 Peter, what is God's desire regarding people perishing?
options: He doesn't want anyone to perish
hint: God is patient and loving toward all people.
explanation: 2 Peter 3:9 states that God 'is patient with you, not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance.'

question: What biblical event does Peter use as an example of God's judgment?
hint: This event involved water covering the whole earth.
explanation: In 2 Peter 2:5 and 3:6, Peter references Noah's flood as an example of God's judgment on the ungodly world.

question: What does Peter say will happen to the heavens and earth in the future?
hint: Think about what happens when something is destroyed by fire.
explanation: 2 Peter 3:10 describes how 'the heavens will disappear with a roar; the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and everything done in it will be laid bare.'

question: Which Old Testament prophet does Peter specifically mention as being moved by the Holy Spirit?
hint: Peter doesn't name a specific prophet but speaks about prophecy in general.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:21, Peter states that 'prophecy never had its origin in the human will, but prophets, though human, spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit,' referring to prophets generally.

question: According to 2 Peter 1:4, believers become partakers of what?
hint: This involves sharing in God's own character and qualities.
explanation: 2 Peter 1:4 says believers 'may participate in the divine nature, having escaped the corruption in the world caused by evil desires.'

question: What event does Peter reference as his personal witness to Christ's glory?
hint: This event happened on a mountain where Jesus' appearance changed.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:16-18, Peter references being an eyewitness to Christ's majesty on the holy mountain, referring to the transfiguration.

question: Which cities does Peter mention as examples of divine judgment?
hint: These cities were destroyed by fire and sulfur from heaven.
explanation: In 2 Peter 2:6, Peter mentions that God 'condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah by burning them to ashes, and made them an example of what is going to happen to the ungodly.'

question: What does Peter say about Paul's letters?
options: They are too difficult to understand
They contain wisdom but some parts are hard to understand
hint: Peter acknowledges both the value and the difficulty of Paul's writings.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:15-16, Peter acknowledges that Paul writes with wisdom but notes that 'his letters contain some things that are hard to understand.'

question: In the Greek concept underlying 2 Peter 1:4, what does 'partakers of the divine nature' (κοινωνοὶ θείας φύσεως) primarily emphasize?
hint: This concept relates to spiritual and moral transformation rather than ontological change.
explanation: The Greek term κοινωνοὶ (koinonoi) suggests fellowship and participation. In context, this refers to moral and spiritual transformation through God's promises, not literal deification, as emphasized by the preceding context about escaping worldly corruption.

question: What eschatological framework does Peter employ in chapter 3 regarding the delay of the parousia?
options: Conditional eschatology based on human response
hint: Peter explains the delay in terms of God's character and desire for salvation.
explanation: Peter explains the apparent delay of Christ's return (parousia) in terms of God's patience and desire for repentance (3:9), rather than abandonment of the promise or chronological scheduling, addressing scoffers who questioned the second coming.

question: The phrase 'Scripture cannot be broken' (λύθῆναι) in the context of 2 Peter's discussion of prophecy primarily refers to what hermeneutical principle?
hint: Peter emphasizes that prophecy's origin and interpretation are not matters of private opinion.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:20, Peter states that 'no prophecy of Scripture came about by the prophet's own interpretation (ἐπιλύσεως)' emphasizing that both the origin (v.21) and proper understanding of Scripture require divine guidance, not private interpretation.

question: What does Peter call himself at the beginning of this letter?
hint: He uses two titles to describe his role.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:1, Peter identifies himself as 'Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ.'

question: What does Peter say will happen to false teachers?
hint: Peter warns about their final outcome.
explanation: In 2 Peter 2:1, Peter warns that false teachers 'will secretly introduce destructive heresies' and face destruction.

question: According to Peter, what quality should believers add to their faith first?
hint: It comes right after faith in Peter's list.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:5, Peter instructs believers to 'add to your faith goodness; and to goodness, knowledge.'

question: What does Peter say about God's promises?
options: They are precious and very great
hint: Peter emphasizes their value and importance.
explanation: In 2 Peter 1:4, Peter describes God's promises as 'precious and very great promises.'

question: Which Old Testament figure does Peter mention as an example of God rescuing the godly?
hint: This person lived in a city known for wickedness.
explanation: In 2 Peter 2:7-8, Peter mentions that God 'rescued Lot, a righteous man, who was distressed by the depraved conduct of the lawless.'

question: What does Peter say about the day of the Lord's coming?
options: It will come like a thief
hint: It emphasizes the unexpected nature of this event.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:10, Peter states 'But the day of the Lord will come like a thief.'

question: According to Peter, what is one day with the Lord like?
hint: Peter quotes from the Psalms about God's perspective on time.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:8, Peter writes 'With the Lord a day is like a thousand years, and a thousand years are like a day.'

question: What does Peter say will happen to the elements when the heavens disappear?
options: They will melt in the heat
hint: Peter describes intense heat affecting matter.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:10, Peter describes that 'the elements will be destroyed by fire, and the earth and everything done in it will be laid bare.'

question: What does Peter say believers should be eager to do?
hint: It relates to their spiritual condition when Christ returns.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:14, Peter urges believers to 'make every effort to be found spotless, blameless and at peace with him.'

question: In the context of 2 Peter 2:15, which Old Testament figure is referenced regarding the 'way of Balaam'?
hint: The correct patronymic appears in Numbers 22.
explanation: 2 Peter 2:15 refers to 'the way of Balaam son of Beor, who loved the wages of wickedness,' matching the identification in Numbers 22:5.

question: What theological concept does Peter employ when he states that scoffers will come 'following their own evil desires'?
hint: This relates to end-times doubt motivated by sinful inclinations.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:3, Peter connects eschatological skepticism with moral corruption, showing how ethical compromise leads to doctrinal error regarding Christ's return.

question: The term 'epignosis' (ἐπίγνωσις) appears multiple times in 2 Peter. What does this concept specifically denote?
hint: This Greek term suggests deeper, more complete understanding than basic 'gnosis.'
explanation: Peter uses 'epignosis' (2 Peter 1:2, 1:3, 1:8, 2:20) to denote full, experiential knowledge of God and Christ, emphasizing intimate acquaintance rather than mere intellectual awareness.

question: According to 2 Peter, what should we remember about God when people mock the promise of Jesus' coming?
options: God is slow about His promise
God is patient, not wanting anyone to perish
hint: Think about God's character and His heart for people.
explanation: In 2 Peter 3:9, Peter explains that God is not slow in keeping His promise, but is patient with us, not wanting anyone to perish, but everyone to come to repentance.

question: According to 1 John, what cleanses us from all sin?
hint: It refers to Jesus' sacrifice on the cross.
explanation: 1 John 1:7 teaches that 'the blood of Jesus, his Son, purifies us from all sin,' referring to Christ's atoning sacrifice.

question: Who wrote the book of 1 John?
hint: He was one of Jesus' twelve disciples and also wrote a Gospel.
explanation: John the Apostle, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, is traditionally recognized as the author of 1 John, along with the Gospel of John and Revelation.

question: According to 1 John, what is God?
hint: This is one of the most famous statements about God's nature in the Bible.
explanation: 1 John 4:8 and 4:16 both declare that 'God is love,' emphasizing God's essential nature and character.

question: What does 1 John say about walking in darkness?
options: It means we lie and do not live out the truth
hint: Darkness is contrasted with light and truth in this book.
explanation: 1 John 1:6 states that if we claim to have fellowship with God yet walk in the darkness, we lie and do not live out the truth.

question: What major heretical teaching does John address in this letter?
hint: This heresy denied that Jesus came in the flesh and claimed special knowledge.
explanation: John addresses early Gnostic teachings that denied Jesus came in the flesh (1 John 4:2-3) and claimed to have special spiritual knowledge while living in sin.

question: What are the three things that testify according to 1 John 5:8?
options: The Spirit, the water, and the blood
hint: These three elements all point to Jesus' identity and work.
explanation: 1 John 5:8 states 'the Spirit, the water and the blood; and the three are in agreement,' testifying to Jesus as the Son of God.

question: According to 1 John, what is the confidence we have in approaching God?
options: That if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us
hint: It relates to prayer and God's will.
explanation: 1 John 5:14 teaches that 'if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us,' giving believers confidence in prayer.

question: Who does John call 'antichrist'?
options: Anyone who denies that Jesus is the Christ
hint: It's about denying Jesus' identity, not just future prophecy.
explanation: 1 John 2:22 identifies the antichrist as 'the man who denies that Jesus is the Christ' and denies the Father and the Son.

question: What does John say about the relationship between loving God and loving others?
options: Whoever claims to love God yet hates a brother is a liar
We should focus only on loving God
hint: John emphasizes that these two loves must go together.
explanation: 1 John 4:20 declares that 'whoever claims to love God yet hates a brother or sister is a liar,' showing that love for God and others are inseparable.

question: In 1 John's theological framework, what is the relationship between 'knowing God' and 'keeping his commands'?
options: Commands are optional for those who know God
Knowing God naturally results in keeping commands as evidence
Commands help us get to know God
hint: John presents this as a test of genuine spiritual knowledge.
explanation: 1 John 2:3-4 establishes that we know we have come to know God if we keep his commands, and anyone who claims to know him but doesn't keep his commands is a liar, showing obedience as evidence of true knowledge of God.

question: What does the phrase 'sin that leads to death' likely refer to in 1 John 5:16?
options: Apostasy or final rejection of Christ
hint: Consider the context of the letter's concern with false teachers and those who deny Christ.
explanation: Given the context of 1 John's concern with those who deny Christ and leave the community (antichrists), the 'sin that leads to death' most likely refers to apostasy or the final, persistent rejection of Jesus Christ as Lord and Savior.

question: How does John's use of 'propitiation' (hilasmos) in 1 John 2:2 and 4:10 contribute to his theology of atonement?
options: It emphasizes God's wrath being removed
It focuses only on God's love
It shows Jesus as example only
It denies the need for sacrifice
hint: This Greek term has specific implications for how God's justice and love work together.
explanation: John's use of 'hilasmos' (propitiation) emphasizes that Jesus' sacrifice turns away God's righteous wrath against sin, satisfying divine justice while demonstrating divine love, making Jesus both the means of forgiveness and the demonstration of God's love.

question: Who does John say his readers should not love?
hint: Something that is opposite to God
explanation: 1 John 2:15 commands 'Do not love the world or anything in the world' because love for the world is incompatible with love for the Father.

question: What does John say about God's love for us?
hint: Who started loving first?
explanation: 1 John 4:19 declares 'We love because he first loved us,' showing that God's love initiates our ability to love.

question: What does John say happened when Jesus came in the flesh?
hint: Think about what Jesus came to defeat
explanation: 1 John 3:8 states 'The reason the Son of God appeared was to destroy the devil's work.'

question: What does 1 John say about children of God?
hint: God's children show love like their Father
explanation: 1 John 3:10 indicates that loving one another is a mark of being God's children, while not loving shows one is not from God.

question: What does John say about fear and love?
hint: Perfect love has power over fear
explanation: 1 John 4:18 teaches 'There is no fear in love. But perfect love drives out fear, because fear has to do with punishment.'

question: According to 1 John, what happens to those born of God regarding sin?
hint: Being born of God changes one's relationship to sin
explanation: 1 John 3:9 states 'No one who is born of God will continue to sin, because God's seed remains in them.'

question: What does John say about the commandments of God?
hint: God's commands are not heavy for His children
explanation: 1 John 5:3 declares 'In fact, this is love for God: to keep his commands. And his commands are not burdensome.'

question: What does John say about eternal life?
hint: Life is connected to God's Son
explanation: 1 John 5:11 states 'And this is the testimony: God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.'

question: What does the 'anointing' (chrisma) that believers have represent in John's theology?
hint: It's related to spiritual knowledge and discernment
explanation: In 1 John 2:20,27, the 'anointing' refers to the Holy Spirit who teaches believers and helps them discern truth from falsehood, particularly regarding Christological heresies.

question: How does John's concept of 'abiding' (menō) function theologically in the letter?
hint: It describes a permanent, reciprocal relationship
explanation: John uses 'menō' (abiding) to describe the mutual, permanent indwelling relationship between God and believers (1 John 3:24, 4:13), which is evidenced by love, obedience, and right belief.

question: What is the significance of John's use of 'parousia' (presence/coming) in eschatological context?
hint: It relates to how believers can face Christ's return
explanation: In 1 John 2:28, John connects the parousia with believers having confidence and not being ashamed, linking present Christian living with eschatological hope and judgment.

question: According to 1 John, what should we do if we say we have no sin?
hint: Think about being honest about our mistakes
explanation: 1 John 1:8 states 'If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us.'

question: What does John say believers can know about their prayers being answered?
options: If we ask according to His will, He hears us
hint: There's a condition related to God's desires
explanation: 1 John 5:14-15 teaches that if we ask anything according to God's will, He hears us, and if He hears us, we have what we asked for.

question: According to 1 John, what overcomes the world?
hint: This is something believers have in Jesus
explanation: 1 John 5:4 states 'for everyone born of God overcomes the world. This is the victory that has overcome the world, even our faith.'

question: Who does John refer to as his 'dear children' in this letter?
hint: John uses this term affectionately for those he is writing to
explanation: Throughout 1 John, the author addresses believers as 'dear children' (teknía), showing his pastoral care for them.

question: What does John say about someone who claims to know God but does not obey His commands?
options: They are liars and truth is not in them
hint: John uses very strong language about this contradiction
explanation: 1 John 2:4 states 'Whoever says, I know him but does not do what he commands is a liar, and the truth is not in that person.'

question: What three things does John list as 'in the world' that do not come from the Father?
options: Lust of flesh, lust of eyes, and pride of life
hint: These relate to desires and attitudes that oppose God
explanation: 1 John 2:16 lists 'the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life' as not coming from the Father but from the world.

question: In John's theological framework, what does he mean by the phrase 'his seed remains in him' regarding those born of God?
options: God's nature/word abides in them permanently
hint: This relates to the permanent spiritual nature implanted in believers
explanation: 1 John 3:9 uses 'sperma' (seed) to indicate God's divine nature or word that remains in the believer, making continued sinning impossible for the regenerate.

question: The phrase 'chosen lady' in verse 1 is debated by scholars. What are the two main interpretations?
options: An individual woman or a local church
hint: One interpretation is literal, the other is metaphorical
explanation: Scholars debate whether 'chosen lady' refers to an actual woman and her family or is a metaphor for a local church and its members.

question: What is the contextual significance of John's instruction not to welcome false teachers?
options: It reflects the itinerant teacher system and need for discernment
hint: This relates to how early Christianity spread through traveling teachers
explanation: In the early church, traveling teachers depended on hospitality. John's warning addresses the need to discern true from false teachers in this system to prevent spreading heretical doctrine.

question: Who wrote the book of 2 John?
hint: This person calls himself by a title, not his name
explanation: The author identifies himself as 'the elder' in verse 1, traditionally understood to be the apostle John.

question: To whom is 2 John addressed?
options: The chosen lady and her children
hint: It's addressed to a woman and her family
explanation: The letter is addressed to 'the lady chosen by God and to her children' in verse 1.

question: What does John say we should walk in?
hint: It's the opposite of lies
explanation: John emphasizes walking in truth throughout the letter, mentioning it multiple times as fundamental to Christian living.

question: What commandment does John say is not new?
hint: This is about caring for other people
explanation: In verse 5, John writes about the command to love one another, which he says is not new but one they have had from the beginning.

question: What does John warn against regarding deceivers?
hint: It's about hospitality and greeting
explanation: In verses 10-11, John warns not to take deceivers into your house or welcome them, as doing so shares in their wicked work.

question: What does John say about those who do not acknowledge Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh?
hint: John uses very strong language about these people
explanation: In verse 7, John identifies those who do not acknowledge Jesus Christ as coming in the flesh as deceivers and antichrists.

question: What does John say about anyone who runs ahead and does not continue in the teaching of Christ?
hint: It's about their relationship with God
explanation: In verse 9, John states that anyone who runs ahead and does not continue in the teaching of Christ does not have God.

question: How does John describe love?
options: Walking in obedience to God's commands
hint: It's connected to following God's instructions
explanation: In verse 6, John defines love as walking in obedience to God's commands.

question: Why does John say he is writing this letter?
options: So that they may not lose what they have worked for
hint: It's about protecting something they already have
explanation: In verse 8, John writes to warn them so they will not lose what they have worked for, but will be rewarded fully.

question: What is the theological significance of John's emphasis on Jesus Christ 'coming in the flesh'?
options: It affirms the incarnation against Docetic heresy
It proves Jesus was only human
It shows Jesus was adopted by God
hint: This addresses a specific early church heresy about Jesus' nature
explanation: John's emphasis counters Docetism, which denied that Christ truly came in the flesh, instead claiming He only appeared to be human.

question: What reason does John give for supporting traveling teachers?
options: They went out for the sake of the Name
hint: This relates to their motivation for traveling and preaching.
explanation: In verse 7, John explains that these teachers 'went out for the sake of the Name, receiving no help from the pagans,' meaning they traveled for Christ's sake.

question: Who wrote the book of 3 John?
hint: This person was one of Jesus' twelve disciples and wrote several other books.
explanation: The apostle John, one of the twelve disciples of Jesus, is traditionally recognized as the author of 3 John, along with 1 John, 2 John, and the Gospel of John.

question: To whom is 3 John addressed?
hint: This person is called 'dear friend' and is praised for his hospitality.
explanation: 3 John is addressed to Gaius, whom John calls his 'dear friend' and commends for his faithful support of traveling teachers.

question: Who is criticized in 3 John for not welcoming the brothers?
hint: This person loves to be first and refuses to show hospitality.
explanation: Diotrephes is criticized by John for his pride, refusal to welcome traveling teachers, and his attempt to put people out of the church.

question: What does John say about Demetrius?
options: He is well spoken of by everyone
He causes division in the church
hint: This person has a good reputation and even the truth itself speaks well of him.
explanation: John speaks highly of Demetrius, saying he is well spoken of by everyone and by the truth itself, likely recommending him to Gaius.

question: What does John praise Gaius for doing?
hint: This involves welcoming and helping people who are spreading God's word.
explanation: John commends Gaius for his faithful work in providing hospitality and support to traveling Christian teachers and missionaries.

question: Complete this verse: 'Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is...'
hint: John wishes for Gaius's physical well-being to match his spiritual condition.
explanation: In 3 John 1:2, John writes: 'Dear friend, I pray that you may enjoy good health and that all may go well with you, even as your soul is getting along well.'

question: What does John say gives him great joy?
options: Hearing that his children are walking in truth
hint: This relates to the spiritual condition of people John considers his spiritual offspring.
explanation: In verse 4, John writes: 'I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth,' referring to those he has led to faith.

question: What does Diotrephes do to people who want to welcome the traveling teachers?
options: He puts them out of the church
hint: This is a severe action that removes people from the Christian community.
explanation: According to verse 10, Diotrephes not only refuses to welcome the brothers himself but also stops those who want to do so and puts them out of the church.

question: What does John mean when he says the traveling teachers receive 'nothing from the Gentiles'?
options: Gentiles are too poor to help
They only accept support from believers
hint: This refers to their principle of accepting support only from certain people.
explanation: John indicates that these Christian teachers maintain their integrity by accepting support only from fellow believers, not from non-Christian Gentiles, thus depending on Christian hospitality.

question: What does John promise to do about Diotrephes when he visits?
options: Call attention to what he is doing
Write a letter to the congregation
hint: John plans to publicly address Diotrephes's behavior and actions.
explanation: In verse 10, John states: 'So when I come, I will call attention to what he is doing, spreading malicious nonsense about us,' indicating he will confront Diotrephes publicly.

question: What principle does John state about imitating good and evil?
options: Anyone who does what is good is from God
Evil actions separate us from God's love
hint: This verse contrasts doing good with doing evil and relates it to our relationship with God.
explanation: In verse 11, John writes: 'Anyone who does what is good is from God. Anyone who does what is evil has not seen God,' establishing a principle about the source and evidence of spiritual life.

question: Who wrote the book of Jude?
hint: The book is named after its author
explanation: Jude identifies himself as the author in verse 1, calling himself 'a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James.'

question: Whose brother was Jude according to the opening verse?
hint: This person was a leader in the early church
explanation: Jude 1:1 states that Jude was 'a brother of James,' likely referring to James the brother of Jesus.

question: What did the archangel Michael dispute with the devil about?
hint: It involved a great leader who died in the wilderness
explanation: Jude 1:9 mentions that Michael the archangel disputed with the devil about Moses' body.

question: What does Jude say believers should do while waiting for God's mercy?
hint: Jude gives multiple instructions for spiritual growth
explanation: Jude 1:20-21 instructs believers to build themselves up in faith, pray in the Holy Spirit, and keep themselves in God's love.

question: What does Jude encourage believers to do in verse 3?
hint: It involves defending something precious
explanation: Jude 1:3 urges believers to 'contend for the faith that was once for all entrusted to God's holy people.'

question: Which Old Testament cities does Jude mention as examples of God's judgment?
hint: These cities were destroyed by fire from heaven
explanation: Jude 1:7 cites Sodom and Gomorrah as examples of those who suffered the punishment of eternal fire.

question: Which Old Testament figure does Jude mention as an example of rebellion?
hint: Jude mentions three negative examples from the Old Testament
explanation: Jude 1:11 mentions all three: 'Woe to them! They have taken the way of Cain; they have rushed for profit into Balaam's error; they have been destroyed in Korah's rebellion.'

question: How does Jude describe false teachers in terms of natural elements?
hint: Jude uses multiple nature metaphors to describe their emptiness
explanation: Jude 1:12-13 uses all these metaphors: clouds without rain, fruitless trees, and wild waves of the sea to describe false teachers.

question: Which biblical figure does Jude quote as prophesying about the Lord's coming?
hint: This person was taken up to heaven without dying
explanation: Jude 1:14-15 quotes Enoch's prophecy about the Lord coming with thousands of his holy ones to judge everyone.

question: What specific phrase does Jude use to describe the faith that was delivered to the saints?
hint: It emphasizes the finality and completeness of the delivery
explanation: Jude 1:3 uses the phrase 'once for all delivered' (Greek: hapax paradothenti), emphasizing the finality and completeness of the faith given to believers.

question: According to Jude, what did the angels who left their proper dwelling experience?
hint: Their punishment involves being bound until judgment day
explanation: Jude 1:6 states that God has kept the angels who left their positions 'in darkness, bound with everlasting chains for judgment on the great Day.'

question: What does the doxology at the end of Jude attribute to God through Jesus Christ?
hint: The doxology includes four divine attributes
explanation: Jude 1:25 attributes 'glory, majesty, power and authority' to God through Jesus Christ, both now and forever.

question: According to Jude verse 1, who is Jude a servant of?
hint: Look at the very beginning of the letter where Jude introduces himself.
explanation: In Jude 1:1, Jude identifies himself as 'a servant of Jesus Christ and a brother of James.'

question: What happened to the people who were saved from Egypt but did not believe?
options: They entered the promised land later
hint: Jude uses this as an example of God's judgment on unbelief.
explanation: In Jude 1:5, Jude reminds readers that 'the Lord delivered his people out of Egypt, but later destroyed those who did not believe.'

question: What specific prophetic declaration does Jude attribute to Enoch about the Lord?
options: He will establish His kingdom on earth
He will come with thousands of His holy ones to judge
He will destroy the wicked with fire
hint: This prophecy involves the Lord coming with a great company for the purpose of judgment.
explanation: In Jude 1:14-15, Jude quotes Enoch's prophecy: 'See, the Lord is coming with thousands upon thousands of his holy ones to judge everyone, and to convict all of them of all the ungodly acts they have committed.'

question: Who wrote the book of Revelation?
hint: This apostle was also known as 'the beloved disciple'
explanation: The apostle John wrote Revelation while exiled on the island of Patmos (Revelation 1:1, 1:9).

question: On which island was John when he received the vision?
hint: This Greek island was used as a place of exile
explanation: John was on the island of Patmos because of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus (Revelation 1:9).

question: What happens when the seventh seal is opened?
hint: It was very quiet for about half an hour
explanation: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour (Revelation 8:1).

question: Who is called 'the Lamb' throughout Revelation?
hint: This person died for our sins
explanation: Jesus is consistently referred to as 'the Lamb' throughout Revelation, emphasizing His sacrificial death (Revelation 5:6).

question: What does Jesus say He is in Revelation 22:13?
hint: These are the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet
explanation: Jesus declares 'I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End' (Revelation 22:13).

question: How many churches receive letters in Revelation chapters 2-3?
hint: This is often considered a number of completeness in the Bible
explanation: Seven churches receive letters: Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and Laodicea (Revelation 2-3).

question: What do the 24 elders cast before the throne?
hint: These are worn on the head as symbols of authority
explanation: The twenty-four elders fall down before the throne and cast their crowns before the one who sits on the throne (Revelation 4:10).

question: How many witnesses prophesy for 1,260 days?
hint: The same number required for valid testimony under Jewish law
explanation: God gives power to His two witnesses, and they will prophesy for 1,260 days (Revelation 11:3).

question: What is written on the white stone given to overcomers?
hint: It's something personal that only the recipient knows
explanation: To the one who is victorious, Christ will give a white stone with a new name written on it, known only to the one who receives it (Revelation 2:17).

question: What is the number of the beast mentioned in Revelation 13:18?
hint: It is described as 'man's number' and requires wisdom to calculate
explanation: The number of the beast is 666, which is described as man's number requiring wisdom and insight to calculate (Revelation 13:18).

question: What are the dimensions of the New Jerusalem described in Revelation 21?
hint: The measurement relates to the number of tribes of Israel
explanation: The city is laid out as a square, with each side measuring 12,000 stadia in length, width, and height (Revelation 21:16).

question: In Revelation 16, what happens when the sixth bowl is poured out?
hint: This prepares the way for kings from the east
explanation: The sixth angel poured out his bowl on the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up to prepare the way for the kings from the East (Revelation 16:12).

question: Who appears as a rider on a white horse in Revelation 19?
hint: This rider is called 'Faithful and True' and 'King of kings'
explanation: In Revelation 19:11-16, Jesus Christ appears as a rider on a white horse, called 'Faithful and True' and 'King of kings and Lord of lords'.

question: What falls from heaven like a great mountain burning with fire?
hint: This happens when the second angel sounds his trumpet
explanation: In Revelation 8:8, when the second angel sounds his trumpet, something like a huge mountain burning with fire is thrown into the sea.

question: Which city is described as the great prostitute in Revelation?
hint: This city is called 'Babylon the Great' in the vision
explanation: In Revelation 17-18, Babylon the Great is described as the great prostitute and represents a corrupt world system.

question: What does Jesus promise to do in Revelation 3:20?
options: Stand at the door and knock
hint: This involves Jesus wanting to have fellowship with believers
explanation: In Revelation 3:20, Jesus says 'Here I am! I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in and eat with that person, and they with me.'

question: Who are the two witnesses compared to in Revelation 11?
hint: One could stop rain, the other could turn water to blood
explanation: The two witnesses in Revelation 11:3-6 have powers reminiscent of Moses (turning water to blood, striking earth with plagues) and Elijah (shutting up the sky so it doesn't rain).

question: What happens to the dragon after the thousand years are over?
options: He is released for a short time
hint: This is temporary before his final judgment
explanation: According to Revelation 20:7-8, when the thousand years are over, Satan will be released from his prison for a short time to deceive the nations once more.

question: Which church is told they have left their first love?
hint: This church was commended for their hard work and perseverance
explanation: In Revelation 2:4, the church in Ephesus is told 'Yet I hold this against you: You have forsaken the love you had at first.'

question: What does the voice from heaven say about those who die in the Lord?
options: They are blessed and their deeds follow them
hint: This blessing mentions both rest and works
explanation: Revelation 14:13 states: 'Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on. Yes, says the Spirit, they will rest from their labor, for their deeds will follow them.'

question: What comes out of the mouths of the dragon, beast, and false prophet?
hint: These gather kings for the battle of Armageddon
explanation: In Revelation 16:13-14, three impure spirits that looked like frogs come out of their mouths, which are demonic spirits that perform signs and gather kings for battle.

question: What is the specific title given to Jesus in Revelation 1:5?
options: The faithful witness, firstborn from the dead, ruler of kings
The Alpha and Omega, beginning and end
The Lion of Judah, Root of David
hint: This title has three parts describing His testimony, resurrection, and authority
explanation: Revelation 1:5 specifically calls Jesus Christ 'the faithful witness, the firstborn from the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth.'

question: What is the symbolic meaning of the great city where the two witnesses are killed?
hint: This city is given two symbolic names representing corruption and bondage
explanation: Revelation 11:8 describes the great city 'which is figuratively called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified,' indicating spiritual corruption and oppression.

question: What is the specific warning about adding to or taking away from this prophecy?
options: Plagues added and name removed from book of life
hint: The consequences involve both receiving something harmful and losing something precious
explanation: Revelation 22:18-19 warns that God will add plagues to anyone who adds to these words, and will take away their share in the tree of life and holy city from anyone who takes words away.

question: Which church was neither hot nor cold, but lukewarm?
hint: This church was wealthy but spiritually poor.
explanation: Revelation 3:15-16 describes the church in Laodicea as lukewarm, neither hot nor cold.

question: How many heads does the great red dragon have?
hint: This is the same number as the churches that receive letters.
explanation: Revelation 12:3 describes the great red dragon as having seven heads and ten horns.

question: What color is the horse that Death rides?
hint: This color suggests sickness and death.
explanation: Revelation 6:8 describes Death riding a pale horse, and Hades was following close behind him.

question: Complete this verse: 'Behold, I am coming soon! My reward is with me, and I will give to each person according to what they have...'
hint: This refers to our actions and deeds.
explanation: Revelation 22:12 says Jesus will reward each person according to what they have done.

question: Who is described as having eyes like blazing fire and feet like burnished bronze?
hint: This figure walks among the lampstands.
explanation: Revelation 1:13-15 describes the Son of Man with eyes like blazing fire and feet like burnished bronze.

question: What happens when the fifth trumpet sounds?
options: Hail and fire fall to earth
A star falls and opens the Abyss
The sun and moon are darkened
hint: This involves locusts coming from a deep pit.
explanation: Revelation 9:1-2 describes a star falling from heaven with the key to the Abyss, which is then opened.

question: What does the voice from the throne say about God's dwelling place?
options: It is in the highest heaven
Look! God's dwelling place is now among the people
It cannot be seen by human eyes
hint: This speaks of God being close to His people.
explanation: Revelation 21:3 declares that God's dwelling place is now among the people, and He will dwell with them.

question: From which direction do the kings come to battle at Armageddon?
hint: This is the direction of the rising sun.
explanation: Revelation 16:12 mentions that the Euphrates River is dried up to prepare the way for the kings from the East.

question: Who are clothed in white robes and hold palm branches?
options: The great multitude from every nation
hint: They come out of great tribulation.
explanation: Revelation 7:9-14 describes a great multitude from every nation clothed in white robes, holding palm branches, who came out of great tribulation.

question: How long do the nations trample the holy city?
hint: This is the same period mentioned for other prophetic events but in different units.
explanation: Revelation 11:2 specifically states the nations will trample the holy city for 42 months.

question: What does the Spirit say to him who has an ear in each letter to the churches?
options: Listen to what the Spirit says to the churches
hint: This phrase appears at the end of each letter with slight variations.
explanation: Each letter to the seven churches concludes with 'Whoever has ears, let them hear what the Spirit says to the churches' (Revelation 2-3).

question: What is the measurement of the wall of the New Jerusalem?
hint: This number relates to the 12 tribes and 12 apostles.
explanation: Revelation 21:17 states that the wall of the New Jerusalem measured 144 cubits thick, by human measurement.

question: What happens when Jesus opens the first seal?
options: A white horse and rider appear
hint: The rider carries a bow and wears a crown.
explanation: In Revelation 6:2, when the first seal is opened, a white horse appears with a rider holding a bow, and he was given a crown.

question: What does Jesus say He holds in His right hand in Revelation 1?
hint: These represent the angels of the seven churches.
explanation: In Revelation 1:16 and 1:20, Jesus holds seven stars in His right hand, which are the angels of the seven churches.

question: Which city is called the Holy City that comes down from heaven?
hint: It's described as a bride adorned for her husband.
explanation: Revelation 21:2 describes the New Jerusalem coming down from heaven as the Holy City, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband.

question: Who is the angel that holds the key to the Abyss and a great chain?
hint: This angel binds Satan for a thousand years.
explanation: In Revelation 20:1, John sees an angel coming down from heaven with the key to the Abyss and a great chain, but the angel is not named.

question: What happens when the fourth trumpet sounds?
options: A third of the sun, moon, and stars are struck
Fire mixed with blood falls to earth
A great mountain falls into the sea
hint: It affects the sources of light in the sky.
explanation: Revelation 8:12 describes that when the fourth angel sounded his trumpet, a third of the sun, moon, and stars were struck so that a third of them turned dark.

question: Who are the four living creatures that surround God's throne?
hint: They represent different aspects of creation.
explanation: Revelation 4:7 describes four living creatures: one like a lion, one like an ox, one with a face like a man, and one like a flying eagle.

question: What does the voice from heaven say about Babylon when it falls?
options: Fallen! Fallen is Babylon the Great!
Come out of her, my people!
hint: This announcement is repeated for emphasis.
explanation: In Revelation 18:2, a mighty angel proclaims 'Fallen! Fallen is Babylon the Great!' announcing the destruction of the great city.

question: Where do the kings of the earth gather for the final battle?
hint: The Hebrew name means 'mountain of Megiddo.'
explanation: Revelation 16:16 states that the kings are gathered to the place that in Hebrew is called Armageddon for the battle on the great day of God Almighty.

question: Who worships the beast and receives its mark?
options: Those whose names are not in the Book of Life
hint: Their names were not written from the creation of the world.
explanation: Revelation 13:8 explains that all inhabitants of the earth will worship the beast—all whose names have not been written in the Lamb's book of life.

question: What happens during the 'hour of trial' mentioned in Revelation?
options: It tests those who live on the earth
hint: The church in Philadelphia is promised protection from this.
explanation: In Revelation 3:10, Jesus promises the church in Philadelphia protection from 'the hour of trial that is going to come on the whole world to test the inhabitants of the earth.'

question: What is the specific promise to those who overcome in Thyatira?
options: Authority over the nations and the morning star
A white robe and their name in the Book of Life
hint: They will rule with an iron scepter.
explanation: In Revelation 2:26-28, those who overcome in Thyatira are promised authority over the nations to rule with an iron scepter, and Jesus will give them the morning star.

question: What does the phrase 'where also their Lord was crucified' refer to in Revelation 11?
options: The spiritual condition of the great city
The place of the two witnesses' ministry
hint: The city is figuratively called Sodom and Egypt.
explanation: Revelation 11:8 describes the great city 'which is figuratively called Sodom and Egypt, where also their Lord was crucified,' indicating the spiritual corruption rather than literal geography.

question: What happens when the third trumpet sounds?
options: A third of ships are destroyed
A great star falls on rivers
hint: A celestial body affects freshwater sources
explanation: Revelation 8:10-11 describes a great star called Wormwood falling on rivers and springs when the third trumpet sounds, making the waters bitter.

question: Who opens the scroll with seven seals?
hint: This figure is worthy to open the scroll because He was slain
explanation: In Revelation 5, only the Lamb (Jesus) is found worthy to open the scroll with seven seals because He was slain and purchased people for God with His blood.

question: What is the name of the final battle location?
hint: This Hebrew name means 'Mount of Megiddo'
explanation: Revelation 16:16 specifically names Armageddon as the place where the kings gather for the final battle.

question: What happens when the first trumpet sounds?
options: Hail and fire mixed with blood
A great mountain falls into sea
hint: It involves precipitation and fire with blood
explanation: Revelation 8:7 describes the first trumpet bringing hail and fire mixed with blood, thrown down upon the earth.

question: Who gives power to the beast from the sea?
hint: This is another name for Satan
explanation: Revelation 13:2 clearly states that the dragon (Satan) gave the beast his power, throne, and great authority.

question: What does Jesus promise to those who overcome in Philadelphia?
hint: It involves becoming a permanent part of God's house
explanation: In Revelation 3:12, Jesus promises to make overcomers in Philadelphia pillars in the temple of God, and they will never leave it.

question: Which church is promised that Jesus will write God's name on overcomers?
hint: This church is told that no one can shut the door Jesus has opened
explanation: Revelation 3:12 promises that overcomers in Philadelphia will have God's name, the name of God's city, and Jesus' new name written on them.

question: Who are described as having been redeemed as firstfruits to God and the Lamb?
hint: This group follows the Lamb wherever He goes
explanation: Revelation 14:4 describes the 144,000 as those who were purchased from among mankind and offered as firstfruits to God and the Lamb.

question: Complete this proclamation: 'Fear God and give him glory, because the hour of his judgment has come. Worship him who made...'
options: the heavens, the earth, the sea and the springs of water
hint: This includes four specific elements of creation
explanation: Revelation 14:7 contains this exact proclamation by the first angel, emphasizing God as creator of all water sources along with heaven, earth, and sea.

question: How long does the beast from the sea have authority to act?
hint: This period equals three and a half years
explanation: Revelation 13:5 specifically states the beast was given authority to act for 42 months, which equals the prophetic period of three and a half years.

question: What are the foundations of the New Jerusalem's wall adorned with?
hint: Each foundation represents one of the apostles
explanation: Revelation 21:19-20 describes twelve different precious stones adorning the foundations of the New Jerusalem's wall, representing the twelve apostles.

question: What specific blessing is pronounced on those who read, hear, and take to heart the words of this prophecy?
hint: This relates to the timing of the prophecy's fulfillment
explanation: Revelation 1:3 pronounces blessing on those who read and hear this prophecy 'because the time is near,' emphasizing the urgency and immediacy of the prophetic message.

question: What does the phrase 'the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy' mean in Revelation 19:10?
options: True prophecy bears witness to Jesus
The Holy Spirit speaks through Jesus
hint: It explains what genuine prophecy should point toward
explanation: This phrase in Revelation 19:10 indicates that the essential spirit and purpose of all true prophecy is to bear witness to Jesus Christ and His redemptive work.

question: What happens when the second trumpet sounds?
options: A third of the sea becomes blood
hint: It affects the sea and turns it red
explanation: When the second trumpet sounds in Revelation 8:8-9, something like a huge mountain burning with fire is thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea turns to blood.

question: What river flows through the middle of the great street in the New Jerusalem?
options: River of the water of life
hint: This river gives eternal life
explanation: Revelation 22:1-2 describes 'the river of the water of life, as clear as crystal, flowing from the throne of God and of the Lamb down the middle of the great street of the city.'

question: Who is described as having a sharp double-edged sword coming from his mouth?
options: The rider on the red horse
hint: This describes the glorified Christ
explanation: In Revelation 1:16 and 19:15, Jesus is described as having a sharp double-edged sword coming out of His mouth, representing the power of His word.

question: What does the voice say about the merchants in Revelation 18:11?
hint: They have an emotional reaction to Babylon's fall
explanation: Revelation 18:11 states 'The merchants of the earth will weep and mourn over her because no one buys their cargoes anymore' when Babylon falls.

question: What happens when the seventh trumpet sounds?
hint: It involves an announcement about God's rule
explanation: When the seventh trumpet sounds in Revelation 11:15, there are loud voices in heaven saying, 'The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of his Messiah.'

question: What does Revelation 21:4 say God will wipe away?
hint: It's something that comes from crying
explanation: Revelation 21:4 states that God 'will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain, for the old order of things has passed away.'

question: What is the name of the holy city that comes down from heaven?
hint: It's a new version of the city where Jesus was crucified
explanation: In Revelation 21:2, John sees 'the Holy City, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride beautifully dressed for her husband.'

question: Who stands on Mount Zion with the 144,000?
hint: This figure is often used to represent Jesus in Revelation
explanation: Revelation 14:1 describes the Lamb standing on Mount Zion with the 144,000 who have His name and His Father's name written on their foreheads.

question: Who is called the Alpha and Omega in Revelation?
hint: This title means the beginning and the end
explanation: Jesus identifies Himself as the Alpha and Omega in Revelation 1:8 and 22:13, signifying He is the beginning and the end of all things.
